observations.seen: Solid near-black clear color. No starfield, skybox, nebula, or distant bodies.
Low-segment UV sphere with a visibly faceted silhouette, a flat disk ring, two untextured boxes, and squashed spheres for enemies.
No textures anywhere. Every surface is a single flat color.
Uniform matte/unlit-looking materials. The only variation is one blurry specular blob on the planet.
Nothing reads as metal, rock, gas, or ice. There's no roughness variation and no Fresnel.
No visible terminator or day/night side. The planet is almost uniformly lit, so the sun direction is unreadable.
None: no planet shadow on the ring, no ring shadow on the planet, no self-shadowing.
Flat high ambient washes the planet to a pastel. No occlusion or hemisphere tint.
No environment map and no reflections.
Pastels sit in a narrow mid range. No HDR highlights, and the planet looks washed rather than exposed.
The mint/lavender/salmon palette is coherent but low-contrast and toy-like. It doesn't read as space.
Edges are acceptable at 1080p, but the sphere faceting and thin ring edges show stair-stepping.
No bloom, vignette, grading, or chromatic/film treatment.
No muzzle flash, hit, explosion, shield, or trail is visible in any frame, including "action".
None.
Static camera and static planet/ring across frames. Only drone positions change. No rotation, bob, or banking cues.
The player defense is a grey or green box. The player can't easily tell which object they control.
Locked, flat, straight-on orthographic-feeling view with a lot of dead space. No motion, shake, or framing response.
A small centered subject in a black void, HUD hugging the corners, and action clipping under panels.
No parallax, fog, size cues, or lighting falloff. It reads as a 2D diagram.
No planetary atmosphere rim, glow, haze, or space dust.
Pink-on-black enemies are easy to spot, but the player turret, firing arc, threat direction, and shield state are not communicated. Entities hide under the HUD.
Clean card layout and a decent heat gradient bar. However, the "SYSTEMS" panel and checksum are developer/marketing text, and panels occlude the playfield.
Competent sans-serif with a clear hierarchy. Generic, with no game identity.
No feedback for score, damage, or 98% heat. Frames are interchangeable.
HUD covers two-thirds of the screen, the planet renders behind panels, there are no touch controls, and the layout is effectively unplayable.
Placeholder primitives on a clear color with debug UI. Below early-2000s tech-demo level.
